html:
The Cayuse, Umatilla and Walla Walla are three peoples of the Columbia Plateau in northeastern Oregon and southeastern Washington, now joined as the Confederated Tribes of the Umatilla Indian Reservation near Pendleton, Oregon. The Umatilla and Walla Walla spoke Sahaptin languages; the Cayuse had their own language, which has died out.

They fished for salmon on the Columbia and its branches and dug roots. The Cayuse grew rich in horses after about 1700, and the sturdy "cayuse" pony carries their name. In 1836 the missionaries Marcus and Narcissa Whitman settled among the Cayuse near Walla Walla. Measles brought by migrants on the Oregon Trail killed many Cayuse in 1847, and some Cayuse men, blaming the mission, killed the Whitmans and others in the Whitman massacre. A war followed. In the Walla Walla treaty of 1855 the three tribes gave up most of their land for the Umatilla reservation. Their neighbours were the Nez Perce and the Palouse.
